content.value_statement: Notification integrations can expose secrets, mishandle delivery results, or disrupt primary workflows. This skill guides WxPusher implementation with secure configuration, explicit routing, bounded retries, and mock tests.
actual_capabilities: Guide standard POST and SPT integrations using existing project HTTP clients and notification boundaries.
Define UID, Topic, and SPT routing with configuration validation and recipient limits.
Specify top-level and per-target business-response checks, including partial failures.
Plan timeouts, bounded retries, deduplication, and notification failure isolation.
Design mock tests for configuration errors, response failures, rate limits, and content size limits.
Provide troubleshooting, credential-handling, callback, and API maintenance guidance.
limitations: Provides documentation and implementation guidance, not a bundled executable client or notification service.
Live notifications require valid credentials, configured recipients, network access, and explicit authorization.
API acceptance does not guarantee delivery or reading; quotas and client behavior can change.
The references identify no verified public SPT revocation method or Topic CRUD API.

use_cases.title: Add Backend Event Notifications
use_cases.description: Connect application events to a WxPusher adapter while protecting secrets and keeping notification failures separate from primary operations.

use_cases.title: Report Deployment and Monitoring Results
use_cases.description: Add controlled CI/CD or monitoring notifications with protected credentials, bounded retries, and explicit failure policies.

use_cases.title: Notify Personal Script Completion
use_cases.description: Use an SPT POST integration for personal task results, with placeholder configuration and mock verification before authorized live sends.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a First Integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect this project and plan a WxPusher task-completion notification. Use placeholder configuration and identify the smallest implementation and mock test changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: understand the project boundary before implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Implement Standard Notifications
prompt_templates.prompt: Add WxPusher standard POST notifications through our existing HTTP client. Validate UID configuration, check target results, and add mock tests without live sends.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: implement a project notification adapter.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose Partial Failures
prompt_templates.prompt: Investigate these redacted WxPusher responses. Explain partial failures, inspect retry behavior, and add regression tests without exposing secrets or sending live messages.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: troubleshoot response handling and delivery assumptions.

prompt_templates.title: Design Reliable Queue Delivery
prompt_templates.prompt: Integrate WxPusher into our event queue with deduplication, bounded retries, protected secrets, explicit failure handling, and mock tests. Preserve existing business semantics.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: coordinate reliability across asynchronous workflows.

output_examples.input: Add WxPusher alerts when a nightly data import finishes.
output: Integration plan: reuse the worker's notification boundary and send a short completion summary through standard POST.
Configuration: application token and authorized UID list come from the existing secret store.
Verification plan: mock success, target failure, timeout, and missing configuration; live push remains disabled.

output_examples.input: The API returns HTTP 200, but one notification target fails.
output: Diagnosis: HTTP success alone is insufficient; inspect the top-level business code and each target result.
Recommended change: report partial failure and avoid retrying successful targets without deduplication.
Regression test: simulate mixed target results and verify that logs exclude credentials and message bodies.

output_examples.input: An SPT token appeared in a public request URL.
output: Containment: stop using and spreading the exposed token, and remove copies from controlled logs and artifacts.
Revocation status: the references identify no verified public SPT reset or revocation procedure.
Next step: contact the provider for confirmed options; removing local copies does not invalidate the remote token.

best_practices: Prefer JSON POST, approved secret storage, minimal message content, and redacted logs.
Use mock HTTP tests by default and keep live sends within explicitly authorized recipients, purposes, and frequencies.
Validate every target result and enforce timeouts, bounded retries, and deduplication where repeated sends matter.
anti_patterns: Commit tokens, recipient details, or real notification bodies in examples, fixtures, logs, or screenshots.
Treat HTTP 200 or task acceptance as proof that every recipient received or read the notification.
Send unauthorized test messages, retry indefinitely, or silently broadcast when recipient configuration is missing.

faq.question: When should this skill activate?
faq.answer: Use it when the project explicitly selects WxPusher. Generic notifications or requests for another provider are outside its activation boundary.

faq.question: Does this skill include a ready-made client?
faq.answer: No. It provides integration guidance and references for adapting the project's existing language, HTTP client, configuration, and tests.

faq.question: Can implementation proceed without real credentials?
faq.answer: Yes. Use named environment variables and placeholders, then verify behavior with mock HTTP tests. Real sends require valid configuration and authorization.

faq.question: How do UID, Topic, and SPT differ?
faq.answer: UID targets known users, Topic broadcasts to subscribers, and SPT supports simple token-based sends. Their identity systems are not interchangeable.

faq.question: Does a successful API response confirm delivery?
faq.answer: No. Check top-level and per-target business results. Success indicates task creation, not guaranteed delivery or reading.

faq.question: Can an exposed SPT token be reset like an appToken?
faq.answer: The references identify no verified public SPT reset method. Contact the provider; appToken reset procedures do not establish SPT revocation.
